subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this canonical readiness-condition model, plugin readiness provider API, and standard hosting-profile configuration as core, release-tested contracts?
rationale: The RFC creates permanent cross-cutting API, configuration, runtime, upgrade, and support semantics whose scope and ownership cannot be approved from document correctness alone.

options.title: Continue the integrated RFC
options.body: Review conditions, providers, and profiles together while requiring explicit compatibility, support-ownership, and release-conformance commitments.

options.title: Stage the contracts
options.body: Accept normalization of existing Gateway readiness first and defer plugin providers or non-local profiles to follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Keep hosting-specific readiness composition downstream and close the proposal without accepting new core API or configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Continue the integrated RFC
recommendation.body: Review conditions, providers, and profiles together while requiring explicit compatibility, support-ownership, and release-conformance commitments.

likelyOwner.reason: Their repository history introduced and formalized the RFC acceptance process that governs this product-direction decision.
